description: Thinking-first v5 harness campaign (the default from 2026-11-16 on; first for DeepSeek v4.1 Flash). The best-first composite runs first (every harness change believed to help, thinking on), so the headline row exists early; then the composite with one component removed at a time (thinking on), the seed-noise arm, and last the no-thinking counterparts. `campaign.py report` applies the decision rules in `recommend` and states the recommended daily config. Evidence: GLM-5.3-Flash, 2026-11-16, one seed: L0 26/71, A 31/71, B 36/71, and C (B + thinking, wall x2) 18 of the first 21 units against B's 8 on the same units (10 rescued, 0 regressed). Runbook: docs/MODEL_CAMPAIGN.md.

eta.basis: N0 is the 2026-11-16 GLM arm B; GLM's arm A (runner v2, default turns) took 2.1 h at --jobs 4, and B's wall-scaled turns are estimated at +20%. Thinking arms are 2.3x per unit (C vs B, measured on GLM). Pass --base-hours for a model with its own timing; finished arms recalibrate it

arms.label: composite, thinking on (best-first)
arms.note: Everything believed to help: runner v2, wall-scaled turns (G1), thinking on at wall x2 (B's turns, so thinking is not clock-bound), push diagnostics + edit hint + verify-done (G13, G14, G9), packs v2 + host pack (G19, G20), env block (G22) and wall warnings (G23). Escalation stays off (G16: zig-only on the Mac host). The reasoning budget declared is the eval turn cap that bounds thinking (agents/runner.py _EVAL_TURN_TOKENS_THINKING).

arms.label: T without wall-scaled turns
arms.note: The task's own max_iter at the same doubled wall. First ablation: the largest measured harness lever after thinking (B vs A, +5 on GLM), and the one thinking may make redundant (fewer, better turns).

arms.label: T without packs
arms.note: No language pack, no host pack. Second: packs took zig 0/6 to 3/6 on GLM L1, a knowledge gap thinking cannot close, and the host pack targets the ~95 host-friction turns (G20).

arms.label: T without diagnostics, edit hint, verify-done
arms.note: Third: unmeasured on its own before this campaign (v5-harness arm D), with mixed audit evidence (G13 rewrites, G14 rebuilds anyway).

arms.label: T without env block and wall warnings
arms.note: Fourth: the smallest expected effect (a few discovery turns, G22; pacing notices, G23).

arms.label: T under --seed 1 (noise)
arms.note: A Spark server that gets no seed uses a fixed one: every run is one deterministic draw. The composite again under another seed; its churn against T sets the noise margin every decision rule uses.

arms.label: composite, thinking off (daily-latency config)
arms.note: T with thinking explicitly off at the normal wall: what thinking adds to the full harness, and its cost in time and tokens. Thinking is sent as off, not left to the server default, because a model's template may think by default.

arms.label: bare no-thinking baseline (runner v2 + wall-scaled turns)
arms.note: The 2026-11-16 GLM arm B, with thinking pinned off: runner v2 and wall-scaled turns, nothing else. N0 -> N is what the components add without thinking; N0 -> T is everything.

arms.label: T under --seed 2 (second noise draw, optional)
arms.note: Only with --include T_s2: a second seed tightens the noise margin (the noisiest seed arm sets it).

arms.label: T at --jobs 2 --slots 2 (concurrency, optional)
arms.note: Only with --only T_j2 (or --include T_j2): T exactly, at 2 concurrent units instead of 4; the arm's jobs/slots win over the CLI's. Evidence, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3) arm T, 2026-11-18, --jobs 4 --slots 4 (evals/boards/v5/eval-deepseek-v4-1-flash-v5-thinking-first-t-20261118-015132.json): 61/71, all 10 failures on the 3,600 s wall (wall-scale 2); 17 units hit the wall and 7 of them passed on the code left at the kill; 17.0 of 26.6 unit-hours went to wall-killed units. Turns were slow, not scarce: killed units used 8-41 of 60 turns, 470-610 s between events, each turn up to 16,384 tokens at ~30 tok/s per stream with 4 streams (~45 with 2, ~60 with 1; tools/bench.py on the pair); 192_pike_regex spent 8 turns and 3,585 s with zero tool calls. CAUTION, read before the result: run_eval widens every wall by contention_scale(jobs) (4 -> 2.0x, 2 -> 1.33x), so at --jobs 2 the unit wall is 2,400 s, not 3,600 s, and 2,400 s x 45 tok/s = 3,600 s x 30 tok/s: the same ~108K decoded tokens per unit. T_j2 therefore measures whether the contention model holds for this model (a T replay at 2 streams, with less wall for builds and tests), not more tokens per unit; an arm that gives each unit more tokens keeps the absolute wall (--wall-scale 3 at --jobs 2). time_x 2.3 as T (the same tokens per unit); the ETA's jobs scale is 1.33x (throughput jobs / contention_scale), so ~9 h from T's 6.8 h.

arms.label: T + 8192 thinking cap + act nudge (harness9)
arms.note: Only with --only T2 (or --include T2); needs a harness9 tree (the PR that adds OPENBEAST_AGENT_ACT_NUDGE). Arm T2 = T + an 8,192-token per-turn cap (OPENBEAST_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS=8192, declared as --reasoning-budget 8192; the capped-think recovery hands the reasoning tail back as before) + the act nudge (OPENBEAST_AGENT_ACT_NUDGE=1: from the second turn in a row without a tool call, or the first that ends neither capped nor as a final answer, the next reply must be a tool call). Evidence, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3) arm T, 2026-11-18: all 10 failures on the wall; turns of up to 16,384 tokens at ~30 tok/s took 470-610 s each; 192_pike_regex spent 8 turns and 3,585 s, every turn capped, zero tool calls. Half the cap halves a stalled turn (~4-5 min instead of ~9) and the nudge turns idle thinking into a write or a test. The partial stats on a wall kill and the eval fetch guard ship in the same PR and apply to every arm run on a harness9 tree; they change no verdict. Runs at --jobs 4 --slots 4 like T (decided 2026-11-18): the unit wall is T's 3,600 s and the decoded tokens per unit match T's, so T2 vs T isolates the cap and the nudge (T_j2 would only replay T at 2 streams, contention_scale keeping tokens per unit equal). time_x 2.3 as T; ~6.8 h for DeepSeek (T took 6.76 h).

arms.label: T2 with a 4096-token thinking cap (harness9, config only)
arms.note: Only with --only T3. T2 with the per-turn cap halved again (OPENBEAST_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS=4096, declared --reasoning-budget 4096); same harness9 tree and era as T2, so T3 vs T2 isolates the cap. Evidence, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3), 2026-11-19: T2 (cap 8192 + act nudge) scored 65/71 against T's 61/71 (cap 16384, no nudge): +4 (168_kv_e, 173, 183, 190), 0 regressions; gaps between turns fell from 470-610 s to 280-330 s. The remaining failures still hit the 3,600 s wall while capping: 192_pike_regex capped 10 of 21 turns (7 nudges, now 10 tool calls against T's 0); 168_kv_a/c capped 6 times each in 32-33 turns. A 4096 cap halves a capped turn again (~2.5 min) at the risk of cutting reasoning a hard step needs: the measured question is whether faster iteration beats deeper single turns for this model. time_x 2.3 as T (T2 took 6.2 h).

arms.label: T2 with the forced-act turn instead of the act nudge + done-when-verified, 16384 cap (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only U; needs a harness10 tree. Arm U = T2's settings with the act nudge replaced by the forced-act turn (OPENBEAST_AGENT_FORCE_ACT=1, OPENBEAST_AGENT_FORCE_ACT_AFTER=2: after 2 capped thinking turns in a row with no tool call, the next request goes out with enable_thinking=false and asks for 'Decisions so far / Rejected options' then the tool call in the same reply; the lists stay in the history as content, thinking resumes the turn after), plus done-when-verified (OPENBEAST_AGENT_DONE_VERIFIED=1: once a brute force on small inputs and a timing run at the stated limits pass, call task_done; it names G9's re-run check instead of restating it), plus the web tools left out of the prompt and the tool list under eval (OPENBEAST_AGENT_HIDE_WEB=1; they were refused anyway). Cap 16384 (T's), declared --reasoning-budget 16384: the investigation found that T2's 8192 doubled the caps without ending the stalls, and a forced act ends a stall whatever the cap, so the longer cap keeps the deeper single turns; T2 still scored best overall (65 vs T's 61), so U_8k answers the cap question alongside, and T3 (4096, running) measures its direction. Evidence, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3), investigation of 168_linearizability_kv (2026-11-19): it fails 168 mostly by choosing a global memoised search, which times out, instead of the per-key search the problem needs (linearizability is local; the passing files cite it); in a live probe it reasoned to 'decompose by key?' and rejected it by argument. With thinking on it stalls: in T, 314 of 360 unit-minutes went into turns capped with only reasoning (16K cap) and 4 of 6 units never wrote a file; in T2 (8K cap + act nudge) 247 of 360. The text act nudge was ignored every time (up to 11 nudges): with thinking on the model always thinks first and hits the cap again. Each cap discards ~90% of the reasoning (~65K chars generated, ~6K of tail handed back), so the design is re-decided every turn. Passing runs built brute-force checkers; T_s1 168_kv_a kept editing a passing file for ~33 minutes (no task_done). Every harness10 arm also logs the reasoning text of each turn (size-capped) to the transcript. Compare with T2 (65/71). time_x 2.3 as T2 (T2 took 6.2 h; T 6.76 h): ETA ~6-7 h for DeepSeek at --jobs 4.

arms.label: U with an 8192-token thinking cap (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only U_8k. U exactly, with T2's 8192 per-turn cap (OPENBEAST_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS=8192, declared --reasoning-budget 8192). U vs U_8k is the cap question under the forced-act turn: T2 (8192) scored 65 against T's 61 (16384), but the 168 investigation found the 8192 cap doubled the capped turns without ending the stalls (247 of 360 unit-minutes still in reasoning-only caps). With a forced act after 2 caps, a stall costs 2 capped turns + 1 short turn: ~2 x 4.5 min at 8192 against ~2 x 9 min at 16384, so U_8k iterates faster and U thinks deeper per turn. Read with T3 (T2 at 4096). time_x 2.3 (~6.2 h, as T2).

arms.label: U + planning lines (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only UP. U + three general planning lines in the system prompt (OPENBEAST_AGENT_ALGO_LINES=1; agents/runner.py ALGO_LINES, naming no task): bound first (worst-case state count from the stated limits); implement a doubtful simplification (independent parts, a greedy choice, a dropped constraint) and check it against a brute force on many small random inputs before rejecting it; a >5x miss on the time limit means redesign, not micro-optimisation. Evidence: on 168 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3) rejected the per-key split by argument and timed out on a global search; the passing runs built brute-force checkers. UP vs U isolates the lines. Built on U (cap 16384); if U_8k beats U, re-run UP on U_8k's cap. GLM control: run UP for GLM-5.3-Flash too (--only UP --model-name GLM-5.3-Flash, when the pair serves GLM), to tell a DeepSeek-specific effect from a general one. time_x 2.3 (~6-7 h).

arms.label: UP + the algorithmic procedure pack (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only UPA. UP + the frozen language-independent algorithmic procedure pack (OPENBEAST_ALGO_PACK=1: agents/packs/algo-v1.md, ~400 tokens, sha256 6c5324007750c44091a03c98cfef813cac0f3e576f982beb8908c0732e2ac09d, pinned by tests/test_eval_arms_u.py and checked at run start), appended to every unit's pack file after the zig and host packs (it rides the packs channel, so packs stay on as in T). Procedure only, no noun from any v5 unit: bound before code (~1e7 ops/s Python, ~1e9 compiled); decompose into parts that never interact; test doubtful simplifications against a brute force; search over orders/subsets as DFS memoised on the minimal state that determines the future, candidates restricted by guaranteed bounds; standard reductions (sweep, prefix sums, binary search on the answer, bitmask DP to ~20, meet-in-the-middle to ~40); two-stage verification (tiny brute force, then timing at full limits with adversarial shapes); redesign on a >5x miss. UPA vs UP isolates the pack; the pack changes the pack1 cache component of every unit. time_x 2.3 (~6-7 h).

arms.label: UP at an 8192 cap (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only UP_8k. UP with the per-turn cap at 8192 (T2's), so UP_8k vs U_8k isolates the planning lines and UP_8k vs T2 measures the full process+planning stack at the cap that scored best. Evidence, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3), 2026-11-20: U (16384 cap) scored 59/71 against T2's 65 (8192); four of the six units U lost ran out of wall with 11-26 turns against T2's 28-49 (175 hit the wall at 53 turns; 190 used its 60 turns), and all 24 forced turns ended in a tool call, so the 16384 cap, not the forced-act turn, cost U (docs/reports/V5_DEEPSEEK_CAMPAIGN-2026-11-20.md). time_x 2.3.

arms.label: UPA at an 8192 cap (harness10)
arms.note: Only with --only UPA_8k. UPA (UP + the frozen algorithmic pack) at T2's 8192 cap; UPA_8k vs UP_8k isolates the pack. Same evidence as UP_8k. time_x 2.3.

arms.label: T2 for Hy4-flash (NVFP4): the T2-equivalent composite, thinking at reasoning_effort high
arms.note: Only with --only H_T2 (or a campaign run whose --model-name starts with Hy4-flash: recommend.composite_by_model); needs a harness9 tree, as T2. A public-interest measurement: Tencent's Hy4-flash (atakans/Hy4-flash-NVFP4 @ 30f201ac, vLLM TP2 + expert parallel over the pair, DFly drafter 5; docs/SPARK_HYDRA.md 'Hy4-flash (NVFP4, vLLM TP2): staged'), served with `beast-spark hy4`. Compare with DeepSeek's DS-T2 (65/71) under the same harness: H_T2 is T2 exactly (the 8,192-token per-turn cap declared as --reasoning-budget 8192, the act nudge, every T switch), so the two rows differ in the model only. Thinking: the runner sends chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=true for --thinking on (agents/runner.py, era-hashed, unchanged); Hy4's chat template ignores enable_thinking and defaults reasoning_effort to 'high' when the request names none, and vLLM's hy_v4 reasoning parser defaults to the same 'high', so this arm thinks at reasoning_effort high with no per-model mapping. Thinking OFF is NOT reachable this way (enable_thinking=false is ignored too: Hy4 needs reasoning_effort no_think), so N, N0 and the U arms' forced-act turn would still think on Hy4; they are not Hy4 arms until the runner can send reasoning_effort (an era change). served_model: preflight refuses this arm unless the server serves Hy4-flash-NVFP4. ETA UNVERIFIED: Hy4 decodes ~15 tok/s plain, 17-38 with DFly for one stream (CLAIMED), against DeepSeek's ~30 per stream at 4 (T2 took 6.2 h); budget 8-12 h.

arms.label: T2 for the RTX 5090 default (Qwen3.8 27B Uncensored MTP Q5_K_M) at one stream
arms.note: Only with --only Q_T2 (or a campaign run whose --model-name starts with Qwen3.8 27B Uncensored MTP: recommend.composite_by_model); needs a harness9 tree, as T2. Max 2026-11-22: a full 71-unit run of the best composite on the RTX 5090 rig, after its bare L0 baseline (board row Q38U-L0, 39/71) and the profile's L1/L2 diagnostics. T2's switches exactly (the 8,192-token per-turn cap declared as --reasoning-budget 8192, the act nudge, every T assist, wall-scaled turns, thinking on at wall x2); only the concurrency differs: the rig's llama-server serves ONE stream (the shipped 262K-context profile; L0 ran --jobs 1 --slots 1), so four units would queue on one slot and lose wall clock to waiting. served_model: preflight refuses this arm unless the rig's server serves the Q5 default. Harness host: the rig's eval-host container (scripts/eval-host-container.sh), calibrated by a DeepSeek T2 rerun on harness9 (era 036638dd), run 2026-11-22 and finished 2026-11-23 (docs/reports/V5_EVAL_HOST_CALIBRATION-2026-11-23.md). Q_T2 is harness9 like DS-T2, while the bare baseline Q38U-L0 is harness10 (era 9bcd5aa6): any Q_T2 vs Q38U-L0 comparison crosses an era as well as the arm. ETA UNVERIFIED: L0 took 8.0 h at one stream; time_x 2.3 gives ~18 h.

arms.label: T2 for Hy4-flash-abliterated (OrcaRouter Mix-256G GGUF, llama.cpp RPC over the pair)
arms.note: Only with --only HG_T2 (its recommend.composite_by_model entry was removed when the arm was abandoned, 2026-11-23); needs a harness9 tree, as T2. Max 2026-11-22: benchmark the OrcaRouter abliterated GGUF (orcarouter/Hy4-flash-abliterated-GGUF @ 3fd6454b, Mix-256G, six shards sha256-verified against the Hub) with Hy4's best setup. H_T2's settings exactly (T2's switches, --jobs 4 --slots 4), so HG_T2 vs HY4-T2 differs in weights (abliterated mixed-precision GGUF vs stock NVFP4) and engine (llama.cpp PR #32517 fork @ cf70454 with two local patches, RPC across the pair, vs vLLM TP2 + DFly drafter): a model-and-serving row, not an ablation. Thinking: the served template defaults reasoning_effort to high (a local shim maps enable_thinking=false to no_think; T2 sends thinking on, so the shim is inert here). Speed (bring-up 2026-11-23): 8.5 tok/s for 1 stream, 5.3 per stream at 4 (21.3 aggregate) vs vLLM NVFP4's 31.4 / 77.8, so expect many wall-bound units. served_model: preflight refuses this arm unless the pair serves Hy4-flash-abliterated-Mix-256G. ETA UNVERIFIED: 12-20 h. ABANDONED 2026-11-23 (Max): stopped at 16/71 units (8 passed), 10 of them at the 3,600 s wall, 5 with no solution file written; at 5.3 tok/s per stream an 8K thinking turn takes ~25 min, so the row would measure the llama.cpp RPC serve speed more than the model. Not a board row; this model is not tested. The serve recipe (fork cf70454 + two local patches: RPC supports_op for indexer shapes, a 16-head indexer case) and its notes stay on spark-1 in ~/openbeast-runs/.

arms.label: GLM's best (arm C) for Hy4-flash (NVFP4): thinking on, wall-scaled turns, wall x2, no assists, the 16,384-token eval turn cap (no 8K cap or act nudge)
arms.note: Max 2026-11-21: run after H_T2, as an ablation. GLM-5.3-Flash's best configuration (v5-harness arm C: runner v2 + wall-scaled turns (B) + thinking on at wall x2), with every T assist off (the common block's defaults: no diagnostics, edit hint, verify-done, packs, env block or wall warnings) and no 8,192-token cap or act nudge (the 16,384-token eval turn cap only, as GLM-C). Run it on the same harness9 tree as H_T2 (--arm-tree H_C=<harness9 checkout>), so H_T2 vs H_C on Hy4 isolates the T2 additions (assists + 8K cap + nudge) on one model and one harness. Thinking as H_T2: reasoning_effort high by Hy4's default. Only with --only H_C. ETA as H_T2.

recommend.composite_by_model_note: Per-model best-first composite (2026-11-19). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Mia EXL3): T2 (T + 8192-token per-turn cap + act nudge) scored 65/71 against T's 61/71, +4 / 0 regressions (board row DS-T2), so a DeepSeek campaign runs T2 first and `campaign.py report` starts the recommended daily config from T2; each ablation still compares with T, the arm it removes from. T itself is unchanged (the GLM history depends on it). Daily equivalent: AGENT_PROFILE=deepseek-best in openbeast.conf (docs/SPARK_HYDRA.md). Hy4-flash (NVFP4): H_T2, which is T2 exactly against the Hy4 server (staged 2026-11-19; measured 2026-11-21/22 at 60/71, board row HY4-T2), so its row compares with DS-T2.
